newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - April 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - April 9.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from the German press and from Reuters on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products, the Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING, MARKETING & BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS

MUNICH - The Hamburg superior court has once again prohibited an advertising campaign by Munich digital television network DF1, says the Premiere channel. The court issued a temporary restraining order, preventing DF1 from running an ad for subscriptions to its feature film channel "Cinedom". (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Hamburg-based pay-TV network Premiere has received pitches from five advertising agencies. Presentations will take place this week and next week. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Boebel/Adam, Consell, Tostmann & Wulfes and Cayenne advertising agencies will pitch to Honda Motor Co in attempt to win London-based CDP's corporate campaign. (Horizont)

FRANKFURT - Internet euphoria in Germany has ebbed slightly in the advertising field. Although the number of German users in 1996 climbed from two million to 3.8 million, potential online advertisers have had cold feet. Industry sources estimate only five million marks ($2.9 million) in Internet advertising was sold in 1996, well below expectations. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Tchibo Holding AG cannot yet specify details of implementing its purchase of Bremen-based coffee roasting firm Eduscho GmbH & Co, a spokeswoman says, after the cartel authority approved the merger. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Police probing an attempt to blackmail a German food manufacturer say they have discovered two tubes of mustard laced with cyanide in two separate German supermarkets. Police say they discovered the mustard in stores in Saarbruecken in the southwest and Regensburg in the southeast, planted to force mustard manufacturer Thomy, a unit of Switzerland's Nestle, to pay a large sum of money. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Commerzbank says it plans to open 20 small branches in supermarkets, following competitor Deutsche Bank's emergence there. The first will open at the end of April at an Allkauf chain market in Dortmund. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Telecommunications company WorldCom GmbH says it plans to focus on services for large companies in the German market. (Reuter)
COLOGNE - German retail giant Metro AG has made an offer of 150 marks a share to buy out the remaining minority shareholders in supermarket chain Massa AG, Massa says. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

HAMBURG - Hamburg publishing group Milchstrasse says it is aiming for a 10-percent boost in sales in 1997 to 360 million marks, after posting 14.4 percent growth in 1996 to 330 million marks in sales. (Handelsblatt)

ZURICH - Swiss publishing house Ringier plans to reestablish a base in the United States, says chief executive Michael Ringier. The company sold its U.S. unit Ringier America in 1996 and now wants a new but smaller foothold across the Atlantic, Ringier says. (Reuter)

MUNICH - German all-sports television channel DSF has won the broadcasting rights for the Wimbledon and US Open tennis tournaments for 1997 and 1998. The matches will also appear on Kirch group's digital network DF1. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

Harald Stoeber, distribution and marketing manager for Mannesmann Mobilfunk, will leave his position on April 30 but will stay on in other capacities for the group. His successor in distribution will be Karl-Ludwig Dilfer, current northern Germany branch office manager. Friedrich-Peter Joussen, current manager of product marketing, will take over Stoeber's marketing responsibilities as company assistant manager. (Kress)
Volker Henne has joined the board of the Wernersgruener brewery. His predecessor Peter Mayer left due to differences with the brewery in distribution policy. (Kress)
